figures.title: HTTP acceptance, completion and domain result are separate
figures.description: Caller receives complete 202 acceptance, later retrieves a complete 200 whose representation says rejected; status and framing completion do not decide the business outcome.

figures.title: Response framing determines the meaning of EOF
figures.description: Length-delimited and chunked responses can be incomplete at EOF; a close-delimited response can be HTTP-complete while application content remains insufficient.

figures.title: HTTP client ownership lasts through response cleanup
figures.description: Admission and pool wait precede socket assignment and headers; the caller still owns bounded body consumption or cancellation before resources can be released.

figures.title: Range continuation depends on representation identity
figures.description: A retained abc prefix and If-Range A can lead to validated 206 def, or a full 200 after change; the full response cannot be appended to the old prefix.

figures.title: TLS termination creates separate protocol and trust boundaries
figures.description: Client h2 TLS ends at ingress, which opens a separate HTTP/1.1 hop; backend sees ingress as peer and must evaluate original-caller assertions and upstream protection separately.

figures.title: HTTP/2 stream credit and shared connection credit
figures.description: With A credit zero, B credit 2048 and connection credit 512, A waits and B can send at most 512 DATA payload bytes; HEADERS and TCP have separate constraints.

figures.title: HTTPS versions share semantics but use different transport mappings
figures.description: Separate groups map HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 to TLS over TCP, while HTTP/3 maps to QUIC streams with integrated TLS handshake and packet protection over UDP.

figures.title: QUIC ordering is per stream while other constraints remain
figures.description: A waits for missing offset zero while B can deliver xy from its own contiguous offsets; shared connection resources and QPACK dependencies remain separate possible stalls.

figures.title: WebSocket message fragmentation permits interleaved control
figures.description: After valid 101 opening, text fragments hel and lo surround a ping and pong; one hello message results, and a later close exchange does not certify business processing.

figures.title: SSE event dispatch, reconnection cursor and server replay
figures.description: Blank-line termination dispatches event 7, incomplete EOF does not dispatch its tail, and a new request with Last-Event-ID 7 receives retained event 8 under this server contract.

figures.title: gRPC final protocol status is separate from HTTP status
figures.description: HTTP 200 and two messages precede grpc-status 7 with end of stream; partial results remain observed while final protocol status reports call failure.

figures.title: Compatibility evidence has a writer-reader direction
figures.description: Old-to-new, new-to-old and intermediary rewrite paths are separate tests; each needs wire decoding, field preservation and semantic interpretation evidence.

figures.title: Caller timeout and server action can coexist
figures.description: Service action precedes a response the caller does not observe in time; local deadline cleanup leaves the caller uncertain and does not erase the action or establish retry safety.

figures.title: Network diagnosis needs discriminating evidence
figures.description: Observed boundary evidence leads to competing predictions and a scoped observation; inconclusive evidence loops back without converting uncertainty into a root-cause claim.
